lines.text: The class trip has 24 children. Each bus has 6 seats.
How many buses do we need? Tap a number.
Let us fill the first bus. 6, 12, 18, 24.
Four buses with six seats each. That is 4 times 6.
Nice work. Groups of the same size are what multiplying counts.
Not quite yet. Let us count the seats bus by bus.
Look at one bus. How many seats is that?
A floor needs 23 rows of 47 tiles. Guess first, then find the exact total.
About 20 rows of 50 tiles is 1,000. The exact total should be close to that.
Two quotes, 18 items at 47 and 22 items at 39. Which is cheaper, and by roughly how much?
